why: Regular, balanced eating can support general health, energy, and participation in recovery. No single food is a treatment for pain.

slides.title: Food Supports the Whole Person
slides.content: Nutrition can support general health, energy, and recovery habits, but pain is influenced by many factors and cannot be reduced to one food or nutrient.

slides.title: Support the Work of Recovery
slides.content: Regular meals and enough overall food can support energy, training, sleep, and daily participation. A varied pattern with produce, whole grains, protein foods, and unsaturated fats is a practical starting point for many adults.

slides.title: Avoid Food Fear
slides.content: Labels such as ‘good,’ ‘bad,’ or ‘inflammatory’ can oversimplify nutrition. Your overall pattern, preferences, access, culture, and medical needs matter.

slides.title: Personal Needs Vary
slides.content: Allergies, digestive conditions, diabetes, kidney disease, eating-disorder history, and other concerns may require individualized advice from a qualified professional.

slides.title: Try One Practical Step
slides.content: Choose one gap that matters in your day: a missed meal, limited protein, little produce, or inadequate hydration. Make one realistic addition rather than chasing a perfect or 'anti-inflammatory' diet.
slides.resourceLabel: Canada's Food Guide: evidence-based starting point
